findings.title: Both modern editions erase a source-bound historical scientist
findings.evidence: Both visible blocks use only generic periodic-table wording and both historical_entities arrays are empty. Mendeleev survives only inside source_text and source.data, neither of which is the modern reading text.
findings.impact: Chinese and English agree with each other, but both lose a real historical identity present in the approved source. Neutralizing Soviet wording does not authorize deleting a scientist used in a science-history lesson.

findings.title: The naming-credit correction is inaccurately described as spelling localization
findings.evidence: source_term refers to the Curie couple, while term refers to Marie Curie alone. The reason says 'localized spelling only', which does not describe a correction from joint attribution to individual naming credit.
findings.impact: The visible naming-credit correction is scientifically accepted and explicitly authorized. Its historical-entity explanation misstates the nature of the change; this is not a failure of the naming fact or a request to restore the raw attribution.

sourceCoverage.scientificPayload: Radioactivity as a clue to nuclear structure; accidental discovery; discharge-tube x rays with wall glow; Becquerel's afterglow studies using uranium salts.

Light-trigger hypothesis, black-paper plate experiment, blackening, penetrating action like x rays, cloudy-day drawer/copper-cross arrangement, two-day development, spontaneous emission without sunlight and subsequent investigation.
sourceCoverage.qualification: Unknown radiation is not preidentified as alpha. The raw alpha token occurs once in each visible modern prose stream, in the warning.
sourceCoverage.neutralization: The raw speculative assertion that the discovery would certainly have happened much later is not repeated as scientific fact. Both modern texts preserve the accidental impetus and explicitly retain the role of further experimental checking.

sourceCoverage.scientificPayload: Ionization of air, electroscope discharge, uranium quantity comparison across compounds under the same measurement conditions and radioactivity as an atomic rather than compound-specific property.
Search beyond uranium, 1898 thorium work by Marie Curie in France and other scientists, joint systematic ore research with Pierre Curie, identification of polonium and its connection to Poland.
sourceCoverage.qualification: Identified a new element, not isolated a macroscopic pure polonium sample. The cross-page object stays joined and in order.

sourceCoverage.scientificPayload: Discovery and ray-related name of radium, spontaneous radiation and Marie Curie's naming of radioactivity.
Radium [226] as isotope mass number rather than exact average relative atomic mass; atomic number 88; previously unoccupied table position; alkaline-earth classification.
No stable isotopes from atomic number 83 inclusive upward; explicit non-exclusion of radioactive isotopes of lower-numbered elements.

numericChecks.scope: Visible prose; embedded source snapshots, metadata, section-boundary copies and heading number excluded from the prose token count
quantitativeQualifications: [226] preserves the integer identity but explicitly labels it an isotope mass number, not an exact mean atomic mass.
88 explicitly means atomic number, not atomic mass or an ordinal page position.
83 is inclusive and refers to absence of stable isotopes, not absence of radioactivity below that number.
Different uranium-compound intensity comparisons are qualified by the same measurement conditions.
numericChecks.numeric_changes: Empty in all seven prose objects in both editions; no changed digit identities found.

primaryEvidence.independentFact: Uranium salts were found accidentally to emit spontaneous penetrating radiation that affects a photographic plate; later work distinguished it from x-ray radiation.

primaryEvidence.locator: Opening/naming:40; joint work:50; ionization and quantity dependence:54-58; discovery/isolation distinction:62-70,90-94; alkaline-earth and Mendeleev table:80
primaryEvidence.independentFact: Marie names radioactivity, attributes the discoveries to joint work with Pierre, describes atomic-property and uranium/thorium quantity comparisons, and distinguishes identifying the new substances from the later difficult isolation of radium. The table attribution to Mendeleev is explicit.
primaryEvidence.limit: Historical numerical estimates in the 1911 lecture were not imported into the modern prose or treated as current numerical data.

primaryEvidence.independentFact: NIST gives atomic number 88, mass number 226 and a separate isotope relative atomic mass of 226.0254103(25), alongside the bracketed [226] table convention.

primaryEvidence.locator: Relative isotope mass:13-16; Standard Atomic Weight column:26-29
primaryEvidence.independentFact: The saved NIST notes distinguish an element's averaged relative atomic mass from an isotope's relative mass and explicitly say brackets indicate an isotope mass number.
primaryEvidence.limit: The author's broader wording about characteristic natural abundance is not quoted as though it appeared in this cached source. The modern conservative isotope-mass-number statement is directly supported.

primaryEvidence.independentFact: The 2003 experiment reports unambiguous alpha decay of natural bismuth-209, so its formerly assumed stability is not a stable-isotope exception at the boundary.
